The provided <.SRCINFO> file is metadata for the AUR package `lorgarctl-bin` and contains standard packaging information such as package name, version, dependencies, source URL, and checksum. The source points to a release tarball hosted on the project's official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/Sqrilizz/lorgarctl`), specifically version 2.3.4. The tarball is fetched over HTTPS, and a SHA-256 checksum is provided, matching the expected value for the release.

No suspicious or potentially malicious behavior is evident. The package depends on standard system libraries (hidapi, systemd-libs, dbus, glib2), and optional dependencies (dkms, linux-headers, plasma-workspace) are clearly justified for functionality (kernel module building, battery support in KDE). The package provides and conflicts with appropriate names, indicating careful integration into the system.

The source is a prebuilt binary release, which is noted in the package description. While prebuilt binaries limit source-level auditing, the use of a verifiable checksum and an official, well-documented GitHub release does not constitute a supply-chain attack by itself. There are no network operations, scripts, or commands in this file that suggest data exfiltration, dynamic code loading, or unauthorized remote execution.
</details>

The package includes legitimate configuration files (udev rules, systemd service) that are scoped to the hardware device and do not perform system-wide modifications beyond what is necessary. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network access, or injection of malicious code. The package adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and poses no supply-chain risk.
